articles.title: Scientists “truly astonished” by discovery that challenges Earth’s origin story
articles.description: A new study suggests Earth formed almost entirely from material in the inner Solar System, challenging the idea that water-rich material from beyond Jupiter played a major role. If correct, Earth’s water may have been present much closer to the young Sun than scientists previously thought.

articles.description: A pocket-sized, roughly $100 detector can reveal the invisible stream of cosmic particles constantly passing through Earth and even through our bodies. articles.description: Ancient iron meteorites reveal that some of the Solar System’s first solid bodies were built mostly from tiny heat-forged rock beads called chondrules, while water-rich dust was largely excluded. articles.title: A strange circle on satellite maps turned out to be a 390-million-year-old impact crater
articles.description: An amateur astronomer searching satellite maps for a Quebec camping spot accidentally discovered a massive ancient impact crater. Scientists later found shatter cones that confirmed the 25-kilometer-wide structure was blasted into Earth roughly 390 million years ago.

articles.title: First stellar stream beyond the Milky Way could reveal dark matter
articles.description: Astronomers have discovered the first globular cluster stellar stream beyond the Milky Way, opening a new way to study dark matter in distant galaxies. These faint trails of stars trace a galaxy’s gravitational structure and could eventually help scientists map invisible matter across the universe.

articles.title: The LHC just ruled out another hiding place for quantum black holes

articles.title: These massive stars could explain Webb’s strangest galaxies

articles.title: “We just need to go back” – Uranus’ moon Ariel may have hidden a 100-mile-deep ocean
articles.description: Ariel, one of Uranus’ moons, may once have contained a subsurface ocean more than 100 miles deep beneath its fractured icy shell. The finding, combined with similar evidence from Miranda, suggests the distant Uranian system could harbor multiple hidden ocean worlds.

articles.title: Ancient meteorites reveal a powerful force that helped build the Solar System
articles.description: Ancient grains inside one of the oldest known meteorites reveal that a surprisingly strong magnetic field existed during the solar system’s first 200,000 years. The discovery suggests magnetism worked alongside gravity to help transform a vast cloud of gas and dust into the sun and planetary disk.

articles.title: The secret to growing food on Mars could be fungi
articles.description: Scientists think beneficial fungi could help transform nutrient-poor lunar and Martian regolith into a material capable of supporting crops. By helping plants access nutrients and withstand harsh conditions, these microbes could someday make self-sustaining space farming more realistic.

articles.title: “We found something never seen before” – A dead star is producing a shock wave that shouldn’t exist
articles.description: A dead white dwarf with no detectable disk has somehow produced a powerful shock wave that appears to have persisted for at least 1,000 years. Its magnetic field may be partly responsible, but astronomers say an unexplained “mystery engine” may also be at work.

articles.title: Two astronauts who flew farther than anyone before are taking new NASA roles
articles.description: Artemis II astronauts Victor Glover and Reid Wiseman are transitioning to emeritus status at NASA after their historic journey around the Moon earlier this year. articles.title: James Webb reveals why planet formation is a race against time
articles.description: JWST has revealed that young planetary systems lose their planet-building gas through a changing mix of powerful jets, molecular winds, and radiation-driven outflows. As the disks age and their gas disappears, giant planets face a shrinking window to build massive atmospheres.

articles.title: Blood tests reveal why astronauts get constipated in space
articles.description: Spaceflight may dramatically change the gut within weeks, causing bacteria to break down more protein as food moves more slowly through the intestines. The shift could help explain astronaut constipation and may have wider effects on health, making it an important concern for future missions to Mars

articles.title: This suitcase-sized spacecraft could hear the universe before stars existed
articles.description: CosmoCube will use the far side of the Moon as a shield from Earth’s radio noise to search for a faint signal from the universe before the first stars existed. The suitcase-sized satellite could reveal how the cosmic dark ages ended and how dark matter helped build the first galaxies.

articles.title: Is the universe infinite? The answer gets weird fast

articles.title: Black hole jets may decide the fate of entire galaxies
articles.description: Powerful jets from supermassive black holes can disturb star-forming gas far beyond a galaxy’s visible edge, leaving a glowing trail hundreds of thousands of light-years long. articles.title: NASA’s Crew-13 could go from Florida to the ISS in under 9 hours
articles.description: NASA and SpaceX could launch four astronauts to the International Space Station on October 1, with the Dragon spacecraft reaching orbiting outpost less than nine hours after liftoff. Crew-13 will join Expedition 75 after teams complete a final round of intensive launch-readiness checks.

articles.title: NASA's Perseverance Mars rover finds groundwater, lakes, and hot fluids in one place
articles.description: NASA’s Perseverance rover has uncovered a surprisingly complicated history of water in Jezero Crater. Scientists expected the crater’s Margin Unit to contain lake sediments, but instead found ancient igneous rocks that were altered by water on at least three separate occasions.

articles.title: NASA’s Curiosity rover just hit 5,000 days on Mars and sent back this stunning view
articles.description: NASA’s Curiosity rover marked 5,000 Martian days by capturing morning and afternoon views that were blended into a striking Mars “postcard.” The panorama shows Curiosity, its tracks, and the enormous landscape surrounding Mount Sharp and Gale Crater.

articles.title: The ice blasting from Saturn's moon Enceladus is stranger than scientists realized
articles.description: Enceladus may naturally separate and concentrate chemicals from its hidden ocean as droplets slowly freeze and shatter on their way into space. articles.title: A record-breaking X-ray flash may reveal the birth of a magnetar
articles.description: Astronomers have found strong evidence that some mysterious, minutes-long X-ray flashes are produced when two neutron stars collide and create a magnetar. One record-setting event glowed in X-rays for nearly 10 minutes, potentially opening a new way to find these extreme cosmic mergers.

articles.title: Watch Live: NASA’s Crew-13 could make the fastest U.S. trip to the ISS ever
articles.description: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-13 mission is scheduled to launch four astronauts to the International Space Station on October 1. The Dragon could reach the orbiting laboratory in just 7 hours and 50 minutes, making it the fastest U.S. spacecraft journey to the ISS in history.

articles.title: The early universe wasn’t nearly as pristine as scientists thought

articles.title: Powerful simulations reveal how the first stars changed the universe
articles.description: Ultra-detailed simulations are showing how the first stars lit up the dark Universe and seeded space with elements such as carbon, oxygen, and iron. The MEGATRON project could bridge JWST observations of the earliest galaxies with chemical clues preserved in ancient stars today.

articles.title: Chang’e-6 lunar soil contains a surprising magnetic time capsule
articles.description: Scientists studying Chang’e-6 lunar soil have discovered a previously unknown magnetic mineral in natural Moon samples: a form of metallic iron called γ-Fe.
